title: Glued component bundles with an affine section near their intersections
statement: Let X be a reduced scheme [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-reduced-scheme], C_a → X (a in Fin r) a finite closed subscheme cover [def-weil-closed-immersion], and T the union of the distinct pairwise intersections. Suppose T is finite and every point of T is closed in X. For ample invertible modules M_a on C_a [def-sc-invertible-module] [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], there is an invertible module L on X whose tensor pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback] to every C_a are ample, and a section s of L^1 with an affine nonvanishing open U containing T. No ampleness on X is concluded.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NX, proof first two paragraphs (steps 3-4 of lem-sc-reduced-dim-le-one-ample); Properties 09NV, Varieties 09NE, Limits 09NL

proof.text: Pull T back to each closed subscheme. The preimage is finite because each immersion is injective. Apply the affine-section neighbourhood lemma with W the whole subscheme to each ample M_a. Replace M_a by the resulting positive tensor power, which stays ample by the ampleness criterion: for exponent k>0, raise each section of M^n to its kth power, a section of (M^k)^n with the same nonvanishing locus.

Every distinct pairwise intersection is a subset of T, hence a finite set of closed points. Its subspace is T1 and finite, so discrete. The chosen sections are nonvanishing on these intersections. Glue their invertible modules and sections on the reduced ambient scheme.

Pullback commutes with the residue-field value of a section. The glued section locus pulls back to each chosen affine locus and contains T. These affine loci are closed subschemes covering it. Apply the finite closed affine cover theorem. Transport the section through the canonical isomorphism L.tensorPow 1 ≅ L. The restriction isomorphisms transport ampleness from each powered M_a to the restriction of L. With r=0 the cover makes X empty, and the unit with its zero section has empty affine locus.
